Sam (Sales): Quick heads-up — new POC for an enterprise EAP customer. They want a Private deployment across eu-west-1 + us-west-2, strict allowlist for egress, and minimal ops. Questions from them: can PrivateLink be used 'cross-region' without peering? Do we provide stable egress IPs per region? Any pricing or SLA caveats I should pass back? :thinking:
Amar (NetEng): TL;DR: PrivateLink endpoints are regional. You must either deploy endpoints/connectors in each region or route across a transit solution. We don't provide a single global PrivateLink IP. For predictable egress IPs per region we can allocate static EIP (or NAT GW) on the customer's VPC side or provide our per-region egress EIPs for Private deployments (requires reserved capacity contract).
Sam (Sales): Got it. Customer prefers no peering and no transit gateways (security policy). They asked if we can offer 'regional connectors' + DNS-based failover. Is that a supported pattern?
Elaine (Solutions): Yes — standard pattern: deploy our connector in each region, register region-specific CNAMEs (e.g., api.redwood.customer.eu -> eu-west-1 connector). Failover via Route53 health checks. Works for HA and keeps traffic regional. Downside: customer must maintain allowlists for both region EIPs or use FQDN allowlist if their firewall supports it.
Jess (Security): Note: many enterprise firewalls can't do FQDN for TLS SNI if they require IP-level allowlist. If they insist on IPs only, they'll need a small set of static EIPs per region. We can provide a list of egress IPs for Dedicated/Private deployments but it requires a commitment window (billing + security review). Also we need to scope data residency and audit logs in the contract.
Amar (NetEng): To add: If the customer's endpoints are IPv6-only, we need to clarify environment. Our connectors currently speak IPv4. Options: 1) Customer provides NAT64/DNS64 in their edge so IPv6-only clients translate to IPv4 (recommended), 2) We add an IPv6 fronting layer (non-trivial), 3) Use dual-stack app in their VPC. Which option did they ask for?
Sam (Sales): They said "legacy clients are IPv6-only in some branches" and asked if we support NAT64 on our side. They preferred minimal infra changes.
Amar (NetEng): We don't operate NAT64 for customers by default. We recommend customer-managed NAT64 or an edge proxy in their network. If they need us to manage NAT64, that's an enterprise professional services/engineering change and will affect pricing and SLA.
Jess (Security): Also checklist for them to sign off: 1) Which regions will host connectors; 2) Whether they accept per-region EIP allowlist; 3) TLS termination expectation (we support end-to-end TLS with customer-managed certs on Private deploy); 4) KMS/HSM notes for key custody.
Sam (Sales): Can someone post the example firewall allowlist snippet I can drop into the customer questionnaire? They asked for exact ports and sample CIDRs for our regional egress.
Amar (NetEng): Paste below — replace placeholders with allocated EIPs/regions
```
# Example outbound rules (customer firewall -> Redwood connectors)
# allow outbound TLS to our connectors
ALLOW TCP 443 to 34.210.183.0/24   # eu-west-1 connector pool (example)
ALLOW TCP 443 to 52.11.44.0/24     # us-west-2 connector pool (example)
# Health checks from Route53 / monitoring
ALLOW TCP 443 to 54.239.28.0/32   # optional monitoring endpoint
# If using our managed egress IPs (Private deployment), allow these static prefixes
ALLOW TCP 443 to 203.0.113.0/24   # sample-managed-egress-eip-range
```
Sam (Sales): Perfect. Can you also call out SLA/pricing bullets I can include in the quote?
Elaine (Solutions): Quick bullets to include: - Private deployment pricing includes platform license + per-region connector units. - Reserved egress IPs / static EIP pools are an add-on (monthly commitment). - SLA: standard 99.9% regional availability for connectors; multi-region HA requires >1 connector per region + DNS failover (we recommend 2 per region for 99.95%). - Engineering change (eg, managed NAT64 or custom IPv6 fronting) is professional-services and adds lead time (~4-8 weeks).
Jess (Security): For their security questionnaire, note: - We support customer-managed KMS for keys in Private deployments. - Audit logs available (pull via S3/secure endpoint) for 90 days by default (longer retention is an add-on). - We can provide SOC2/infrastructure diagrams under NDA.
Sam (Sales): Thanks. One last ask — customer wants to avoid opening wide egress to cloud provider ranges. They'll only permit a /24 per region. Can we guarantee that?
Amar (NetEng): We can guarantee a small set of static EIPs for their tenancy if they sign a dedicated/reserved capacity contract. Typically we allocate one or two /32s per connector. If they insist on a /24, we can still support but need to reserve capacity and it will change pricing (we'd treat it like a dedicated egress pool).

Elaine (Solutions): Action items: @Sam — share customer decision on NAT64 vs customer-managed; @Amar — add estimated monthly cost for reserved egress IPs and update the quote; @Jess — prepare a short answers doc for their security questionnaire (I'll help).
Sam (Sales): Will do. I'll loop in the customer and come back with their prefered NAT/peering approach. Thanks everyone :+1:
